source_statement: \abstract{Kai Tak's Runway 13 approach joined an instrument-guided descent to a visual turn over Kowloon. This white paper investigates how turn geometry, aircraft dynamics, wind and runway stopping distance interact, while separating mathematical feasibility from historical validation. Dated survey sheets, aerial photogrammetry and the official CAL605 accident record support an evidence-linked reconstruction whose obstacle and datum gaps remain explicit. A frozen reduced point-mass model supplies complete calm-air and steady-wind approach–flare–stop references. Their separate continuous-time interval certificates establish normalized margins of at least 0.0397 and 0.1507934696816132; corresponding necessary finite-dimensional-family upper bounds remain unmatched. The scenarios leave 254.68 m and 552.77 m of runway under identical illustrative braking, but their difference is not an identified causal wind effect. Published recorder and weather evidence illustrates why constant-wind and constant-braking assumptions cannot reconstruct the accident's operational sequence. Sixteen reproducible scientific figures connect the intuitive mechanics to source-bound calculations and technical derivations. The result is a public-facing research resource, not a historical-clearance finding, near-optimality proof, accident-prevention claim or aviation-safety certificate.}
v5_disposition: Replace abstract catalogue with one final scope sentence; establish synthetic entry and assumed dynamics in Act III.

source_statement: A runway-aligned instrument approach would have pointed aircraft towards a different surrounding landscape. Runway 13 instead used an offset Instrument Guidance System (IGS), followed by visual manoeuvring. The Civil Aviation Department dates the IGS introduction to 1974; it improved runway use in adverse weather but did not remove the final visual requirement \citep{cadhistory,cad}.
v5_disposition: State positively: instrument segment followed by required visual acquisition.

source_statement: The IGS supplied lateral guidance along a localiser and vertical guidance on a $3.1^\circ$ glidepath. In the 1993 report, its localiser centreline is $088^\circ$ magnetic; the runway direction is $135^\circ$ magnetic. Both bearings use the same reference, so their difference is $47^\circ$. That is an angular change in direction on a plan, not a command to bank the wings by 47 degrees.
v5_disposition: Retain immediately after bearings; explain bank in Act II.

source_statement: The certified candidate makes the set with $\eta\geq0.0397$ nonempty. Restrict $q$ to its compact parameter box and $\eta$ to a closed bounded interval containing the valid bounds.
